			<div class="event-presenters"><strong>POWERED BY:</strong><ul><li><a href="https://www.visions.de/" target="_blank">VISIONS Magazin</a></li></ul></div></div><div class="single_event_notes">
				<p>One of the most remarkable aspects of Distant Populations—Quicksand’s first album since 2017’s Interiors—is how timely and prescient the themes running throughout its songs sound at this very moment. Thoughtful, driving, and powerful, like the long-lived band itself, the 11 tracks comprising Distant Populations have an emotional resonance that is only amplified by the events of the past stressed-out, locked-down year. If there is a recurring theme running throughout the new album, it might be this: “Everyone is on the<br />
one hand so connected with each other,” says Schreifels, “and on the other hand is so far apart, and so freaked out about everything.” That seeming contradiction may lie at the heart of what Distant Populations is all about. The title comes from a lyric from anarcho-crust punk band Nausea’s “Fallout (Of Our Being)” about “destitute populations”; because of the singer’s thick accent, Schreifels misheard it as “distant populations” and instantly connected with that concept. “So we’re checking out each other’s social media and we<br />
know what everybody’s doing,” he says, pointing out a sad irony. “But when we’re sitting in the same room together, we’re looking at our phones.” That peculiar duality—our simultaneous existence in individual relationships and as part of mass society—is examined with power and surprising emotional impact throughout all of the tracks here. Cutting and sharp lyrical passages pop out on tracks such as the throbbing “Colossus”: “A new life/ We’re never meant to feel completed/As long as we’re here/It doesn’t matter what for” And<br />
alienation—from whom or what often going unsaid—and loneliness are touched on regularly, whether subtly (“Sometimes it’s better just to keep on traveling” from “Phase 90”) or stated plainly (“Living just around the corner/Share the same existence/Doesn’t make a difference/Deconstructed, isolated” from the closing track “Rodan”). Combine those sentiments with the most sweeping, powerful music the band has ever created, and you’ve got a truly unforgettable, extremely timely listening experience.</p>

			</div><div class="single_event_notes">
				<p>JILUKA was formed in February 2015 with a four member line-up:</p>
<p>Ricko (vocals) / Sena (guitar) / Boogie (bass) / Zyean (drums)</p>
<p>JILUKA expresses a variety of emotions by combining their aggressive metal sound with diverse musical essences and utilizing striking, melodious music.</p>
<p>The band released three mini albums and five singles in a three year period, trademarked by an impressive musical evolution, interwoven with a musical sense indicative of the new generation.</p>
<p>Strongly embossed with the label of visual kei Deathcore from the start, both their growth as a band and a hybrid and metallic intensification resulted in the creation of visual kei modern metal.</p>
<p>Furthermore, they expanded their always energetic live performance endeavors and presented the world with their first full album „Metamorphose“ in 2018. And after that, they challenged themselves to take a new step forward in May 2019 with their brilliantly daring cover album „Polyhedron“, which included a metal version of the nationally recognized hit song „U.S.A.“ and an iconic anime song „Fukai Mori“.</p>
<p>Marking their 5th year as a band with their first best-of album „XANADU“ and an anniversary solo show in February 2020, JILUKA are on the cutting edge of V-Kei modern metal with divided albums „Xtopia“(2020) and „IDOLA“(2021).</p>
<p>In October 2022, the band launched their ultimate new flagship „Electro Gothic Metal (EGM)“ sound with the digital single „BLVCK“ (sound-engineered by Jeff Dunne who’s known for working with Motionless in White, Ice Nine Kills, Emmure, Chelsea Grin, etc). And their following digital singles „OVERKILL“ „VENΦM“(2023), „S4VAGE“(2024), spread the possibilities of EGM. Especially music video „VENΦM“ got over 1.5 million view in the first year on YouTube(https://youtu.be/SnTqDzM43VU).</p>
<p>JILUKA made their first performance in the United States in October at Anime Weekend Atlanta 2023. A month later, it was revealed that they would play at Evil Live Festival in Lisbon, becoming the first visual kei band to perform in the country. Taking advantage of the festival date, the band announced their first world tour 2024 named K4RMA with five solo dates in Europe; in the cities of Warsaw, Bratislava, Cologne, Paris and London which all sold out, plus the Resurrection Festival in Spain / EVIL LIVE Fest in Portugal and a show in Los Angeles in July. Due to the success of K4RMA, they returned to Europe in September with „K4RMA – The Return“, this time with 2 new countries: Italy and Finland, and finishing it with a show in China. A four-date tour in United States will begin in late October, 2024.</p>
<p>In February 2025, they released their 5th digital single „KVLT“.  Starting in March, they embarked on a North American tour with IMMINENCE (22 shows in 3 weeks). Furthermore, in May, they launched their headline world tour 2025 „THE KVLT“, touring Europe in June (including festival appearances at the Czech „ROCK FOR PEOPLE“ and Finland „Tuska 2025“) and South America in July. Subsequently, they began a nationwide Japan tour from late August. (During this Japan tour, the band released their new best album „XNDII“ to commemorate their 10th anniversary).</p>
<p>And 2026 kicks off with the release of JILUKA’s latest EGM digital single „DeViLs.“</p>
<p>In May, they embarked on a nationwide tour headlining a total of 17 cities in the US and sold out 10 of that.</p>
<p>Now, JILUKA with EGM is taking over the world!!</p>

</a></span></div>
			</div><div class="single_event_notes">
				<p>Anstatt sich auf ein einziges Genre zu committen, geht <strong>Lilyisthatyou</strong> in der Musikindustrie mit ihrem verspielten, lauten und teilweise frechen Sound sowie Einflüssen aus Dark Pop, Alt-Rock und elektronischen Hyper-Pop-Experimenten ihren eigenen Weg. Die Sängerin aus dem kanadischen Toronto hat sich auf Grundlage ihrer viralen Debütsingle <strong>„FMRN“ </strong>seit 2021 einen stetig wachsenden Katalog aufgebaut, der mehrere weitere erfolgreiche Songs vorweist. Zwischen der Zelebrierung ihrer Zwanziger, Sexpositivity, Feminismus, Selbstbestimmung, jugendlichem Eskapismus und dem Struggle mit den eigenen Gedanken, den Erfahrungen des Erwachsenwerdens sowie Mental Health adressiert die 25-jährige Sängerin Themen aus ihrer eigenen Lebensrealität. Daraus entstand ein Katalog an Songs, der weltweit mit ihren Fans resoniert, sowie ein organisches Wachstum, das von Konsistenz, Instinkt sowie <strong>Lilyisthatyous</strong> klarer künstlerischer Vision geprägt bis heute ungebrochen bleibt. Den Sprung von Kanada nach Europa hat sie seit ihrer letzten Tournee längst geschafft. Nach einer fast restlos ausverkauften Konzertreise durch Nordamerika und ihrem Deutschland-Debüt im April 2025 kommt <strong>Lilyisthatyou</strong> auf der <strong>THE FLOWERS HAVE FEELINGS TOUR </strong>im Frühherbst für zwei Shows zurück nach Deutschland. Am 21. September ist sie in Berlin und am 25. September in Köln zu sehen.</p>
<p>Dass Musik im Blut von <strong>Lily Davies</strong> liegt, bewies sie bereits im Alter von 13 Jahren, als sie ihre ersten Songs schrieb. Schließlich waren es typische Coming-of-Age-Erfahrungen wie eine toxische Beziehung, Substanzmissbrauch und jugendliches Gefühlschaos, die sie inspirierten, erste Songs in Bedroom-Pop-Ästhetik zu schreiben und ab 2021 zu veröffentlichen. Nach weiteren Singles, die musikalische Einflüsse zwischen Punk-Spirit (<strong>„ALL ABOUT ME“</strong>, <strong>„Purity“</strong>) und modernem Alternative-Pop (<strong>„Moderation“</strong>) aufzeigten, bündelte <strong>Lilyisthatyou</strong> 2022 einige Songs zu ihrer ersten EP <strong>„The Character“</strong>. Nach der Mini-EP <strong>„POP MUSIC“</strong> und den beiden Erfolgstracks <strong>„SIREN“</strong> sowie <strong>„RELAX AFTER WORK WITH A DRINK“</strong> (2023) widmete sich <strong>Lilyisthatyou</strong> 2024 auf der EP <strong>„Painful Euphoria“</strong> Einflüssen aus dem Hyper-Pop. Auf ihrer aktuellen EP<strong> „LILITH“</strong>, die 2025 erschienen ist, hat die Künstlerin die musikalischen sowie visuellen Grenzen ihrer chaotischen Welt erneut abgerissen und neu errichtet. Diesen Weg geht sie auch mit ihren aktuellen Singles <strong>„SICK PUPPY“</strong>, <strong>„BACK PAIN“</strong> und <strong>„DIRT ON MY HANDS“</strong> weiter und macht eines klar: Aus der jungen, frechen, bissigen Provokateurin ist eine Künstlerin geworden, die nicht nur in Kanada bereits als definierende Stimme für eine neue Generation des Pops gilt.</p>
